root_cause: The 'OpenVINO GPU unit Tests' step started at 13:14:27Z and was still running 29291 parametrized GPU gtest cases at 14:31:42Z, i.e. ~77 minutes in, right up against the job's 80-minute timeout-minutes cap defined in job_gpu_tests.yml (line 42). GitHub Actions reported 'context canceled' / 'The operation was canceled.' mid-suite (case 26049/29291, ~89% through), the classic signature of a step being killed by an enclosing timeout/cancellation rather than an application error - there is no gtest FAILED line or crash, just an abrupt stop. The PR's changed files (GGUF frontend fusion passes) are not exercised by this GPU-plugin unit-test binary, ruling out a PR-introduced regression; the suite appears to simply be running close to its time budget on this runner. Independently, the TensorFlow Layer Tests job failed one pre-existing flaky accuracy comparison (test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 with dropout), a signature already tracked 7 times in the pattern database (a284d27dfee44614) and unrelated to the PR's GGUF-only changes.
reproduction_steps: N/A for the iGPU timeout - requires running the full ov_gpu_unit_tests binary (29291 cases) on the same igpu self-hosted runner class and observing whether it approaches/exceeds 80 minutes. For the TensorFlow flaky test: pytest install/tests/layer_tests/tensorflow2_keras_tests/test_tf2_keras_lstm.py::TestKerasLSTM::test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 -k 'dropouts' can intermittently reproduce the small FP drift locally.
recommended_actions: Re-run the iGPU unit tests job; a plain rerun is expected to pass since this was a timeout/cancellation, not a code defect, and the PR does not touch the GPU plugin.

If GPU unit test runs are regularly approaching the 80-minute timeout-minutes limit in .github/workflows/job_gpu_tests.yml, consider raising the timeout or sharding the ov_gpu_unit_tests binary (e.g., via --gtest_filter shards) to leave headroom.

Track the TensorFlow test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 flakiness centrally (pattern a284d27dfee44614, now 8 occurrences) and consider tightening/loosening its comparison epsilon or marking it as a known-flaky xfail until the root LSTM/dropout numerical-drift cause is fixed.
Re-run the TensorFlow Layer Tests job in isolation to confirm only the known-flaky LSTM case regresses before blocking the PR on CI.
prevention_strategies: Monitor GPU unit test suite wall-clock duration over time (e.g., via a CI dashboard) and add slack or early sharding before the suite creeps past the configured timeout-minutes; a suite finishing near 95%+ of its budget is an early warning sign before it starts intermittently timing out. For the TF LSTM flakiness, track it via the existing recurring pattern and prioritize a fix (tighter numerical comparison or deterministic seeding) given it has now recurred 8 times across unrelated PRs.
historical_context: The TensorFlow LSTM dropout accuracy mismatch matches pattern a284d27dfee44614 (7 prior occurrences from 2026-08-27 to 2026-11-05, affecting PRs #37611, #37654, #38168, #39121, #39270, #39286, #39341) and the older related pattern 134f01149f41adcc (3 occurrences in June-July). The iGPU-job-timeout-near-the-80-minute-cap signature has not been previously recorded as its own pattern; related but distinct iGPU/GPU-unit-test Infrastructure patterns include 39e65673e42b712c (runner shutdown signal), 43ea0e2412b6a04f (iGPU job cancelled with no logs at all), and 04b05470e7a3eb58 (bulk GPU test failures with elevated per-test durations on Windows) - all point to recurring capacity/timing pressure on GPU test infrastructure rather than code regressions.
